html:
The Yurok are a Native American people of the lower Klamath River and nearby coast of far northern California, and the state's largest tribe today.

They lived in villages of redwood plank houses, on salmon, acorns, sea lions and shellfish. Wealth, counted in dentalium shells, woodpecker scalps, white deerskins and obsidian blades, mattered greatly, and the White Deerskin and Jump dances renewed the world each year. Their neighbours the Hupa, Karuk and Tolowa shared this way of life but spoke unrelated languages. Yurok is distantly related to Wiyot and to the Algonquian languages of the east.

The Gold Rush reached them in 1850, bringing massacre and disease. A reservation on the lower Klamath, next to the Hoopa Valley Reservation, followed. In the 2020s dams on the Klamath they had fought against were removed, letting salmon return.
sum: The Yurok are a Native American people of the lower Klamath River and nearby coast of far northern California, and the state's largest tribe today.
